description: Actual unequal preaccept replies induce slow-path acceptance at two peers and origin commitment. Before delivering Commit, recover at peer 2 and compare peer 0 next PrepareReply phase to ACCEPTED-or-later.

harness.description: Real proposal, preaccept, accept, accept-reply and prepare handlers with actual codecs in a bounded serial schedule.
semantic_changes: Bounded constructor-equivalent state and in-memory peer streams; no background goroutines.
Direct dispatch of serialized messages and direct recovery entry; pending Commit messages remain undelivered.

legality.derivation: Reuse only the bounded empty-replica and serialized-message helpers after checking entry duties. N=5,F=2,Thrifty=true. Replica 2 first proposes a conflicting PUT and solicits peers 3/4, leaving those messages pending. Origin 1 proposes a second PUT of the same key to peers 0/2. Peer 0 has no conflict and peer 2 has its own prior instance, so real preaccept replies differ. The origin processes those replies, enters the slow path, and produces actual Accept messages. Both peers process eligible Accepts; their real replies match instance and ballot and the stored value attributes are checked. Origin processes both acknowledgments and must attain COMMITTED before admission is emitted. Its resulting Commit messages remain buffered. Replica 2 recovers the known locally uncommitted target and its actual higher Prepare is delivered to peer 0. Peer 0 handles only that promise transition after acceptance, then actual serialized PrepareReply is decoded. All exercised links retain message order and unrelated frames remain in flight. The selected ordering of preferred peers is an allowed permutation; no protocol fields are seeded to accepted or committed.
legality.applicability: Serial local handler schedule with real codec boundaries, no background execution or timing claim. Recovery timer entry is invoked directly on a known uncommitted instance; report phase preservation does not depend on measuring watcher delay.
unresolved: No final recovery-selection handler or global safety endpoint is executed.
alternatives: Origin commitment is an attained prerequisite, not inferred from a sent Accept.
The known VBallot codec omission is retained but not compared or repaired; Status is independently serialized.

grounding.derivation: A matching AcceptReply is counted by handleAcceptReply as successful accept support toward commitment. The receiver stores the proposed attributes on its eligible branch. handlePrepare exports Instance.Status as the phase of that retained support, and handlePrepareReply deliberately treats ACCEPTED as a stronger recovery case than PREACCEPTED. The PreAccept guard and findPreAcceptConflicts comment also protect ACCEPTED-or-later instances from regression. Composing these duties requires an eligible acceptor to represent its retained support as ACCEPTED or later until superseded by another legal value transition. The duty is phase fidelity of accepted support, not an assertion that a particular quorum formula is safe.
grounding.applicability: Same instance and accepting peer, eligible non-stale Accept acknowledged at the proposal ballot; no intervening value change or Commit installation before higher Prepare reports the state.
unresolved: No global agreement or recovery progress conclusion.
alternatives: Local ballot and attributes can be preserved while phase is misclassified.
Equal preaccepted recovery support or a later Commit can protect some wider histories without satisfying this local accepted-support representation duty.

observable_properties.description: A peer whose positive eligible acceptance supported the origin commitment reports an accepted-or-later phase in its next promise-only Prepare reply.

uncertainties: No global decision divergence is measured.
